title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 786–787): X is an oriented topological surface of type (g,ν), S a finite set of marked points, and I ⊂ S. For each x ∈ I there is a group T_x ≃ T. Context makes T ≃ Z, the fundamental group of the circle S_x of directions at x, or equivalently of the punctured disc D_x^*. A topological group G acting on (X,S) carries a central-type extension (136): 1 → T^I → G̃ → G → 1.

The universal case is G = A = Autop(X,S), with the topology of uniform convergence of u and u^{-1}. In the hyperbolic ('anabelian') range 2g−2+ν > 0, the identity component A^0 is contractible. So the extension descends to π_0 and gives (139) 1 → Z^I → T̃ → T → 1, where T = T(X,S) = π_0(A) is the Teichmüller (mapping class) group.

This page does three things.
(i) It names T̃ the 'groupe de Teichmüller spécial' of (X,S), written Sp T.
(ii) For arbitrary G, an action of G on (X,S) is the same as a continuous homomorphism G → A. By functoriality of π_0 it fits in the square (141), G → A over π_0(G) → T = π_0(A).
(iii) By functoriality, the previously constructed G̃ is the pull-back of T̃ along G → π_0(G) → T, i.e. G̃ = G ×_T T̃.

He then turns to the situation where X carries a structure, apparently a local analytic or smooth structure, near I. This is needed to define circles of tangent directions S_x. The next page realises G̃ concretely as pairs (u, ũ), where ũ is a lift of u to the universal cover of the boundary circles S̃_I, compatible with the T_I-torsor structure. The topology is the coarsest making the projections continuous.

In modern terms, T̃ is the mapping class group of the surface obtained by real oriented blow-up at the points of I. Equivalently it is the mapping class group of the surface with |I| boundary components, or the π_1 of the moduli of curves with nonzero tangent vectors at the points of I. The sequence 1 → Z^I → T̃ → T → 1 is the capping/forgetful sequence whose kernel is generated by the boundary Dehn twists. The purpose is the theory of tangential base points for the Teichmüller tower and its Galois/GT action.
errors: No mathematical error. The square (141) carries no extra condition: any continuous G → A induces π_0(G) → π_0(A), so the diagram is automatic and merely records the induced map.

Descent of the extension to π_0 requires A^0 to be contractible (Earle–Eells / Hamstrom), which holds only in the hyperbolic range stated on p. 786. Outside that range the passage from G̃ to a pull-back from T̃ needs separate treatment; the page tacitly assumes the anabelian case.

ideas.what: Extension of the Teichmüller group by Z^I (one twist per marked point with boundary/tangent data), called the 'special Teichmüller group' Sp T
ideas.modern_name: Mapping class group of a surface with boundary / framed mapping class group; capping exact sequence 1→Z^n→Mod(Σ_{g}^{n boundary})→PMod(Σ_{g,n})→1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Birman, Dehn-twist theory; e.g. Farb–Margalit exposition); tangential version in Deligne (1989), Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Teichmüller groups and tangential/infinitesimal data on the Teichmüller tower are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme; the specific name 'Teichmüller spécial' is not known in published texts

ideas.what: Action of a topological group G on (X,S) ⇔ continuous homomorphism G → Autop(X,S); extension G̃ obtained as pull-back of the universal extension along G → π_0(G) → T
ideas.modern_name: Universal extension / pull-back of central extensions along classifying homomorphism

ideas.what: Using a local analytic/smooth structure near I to define circles of directions S_x and their universal covers, realising G̃ via lifts to S̃_I (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Real oriented blow-up; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, tangential base points); Kawazumi/Nakamura for real blow-ups of moduli

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard construction: the mapping class group of a surface with boundary as a Z^I-extension of the punctured-surface Teichmüller group, plus pull-back functoriality. Only the terminology 'groupe de Teichmüller spécial' and the topological-group framing are unpublished details; the mathematics is well known.
transcription_corrections: 'd'action de G sur (X,S)' should read 'l'action de G sur (X,S)'.
Line 1 'que prend ainsi le nom' is likely 'qui prend ainsi le nom'.
'Sp T' is written over an insertion 'l'ext.'; read 'l'ext. T̃ = Sp T de T par Z^I, via G → T'.
'structure d'𝔸. G[?]' is uncertain. It is probably an abbreviation for an analytic or differentiable structure near I, since tangent-direction circles are needed on the next page.
